Level 3 — Components inside the Podman CLI.
Builds, runs, and manages containers locally or via
Core container engine logic. Manages Runtime and all
persistence, locking, events, healthchecks and logging
The entry point of the CLI process. It is used to initialise the
application and assemble the root command from which all
A registry that holds all available commands. It is used to bind
commands to the appropriate container or image engine
A collection of subcommands grouped by resource type. It is
used to expose operations on containers, pods, images,
volumes, networks, and other resources to the user.
A set of shared utilities for the CLI. It is used to provide
common flag definitions, argument validation, and output
The subcommand responsible for starting the REST API server.
It is used to initialise and hand off control to the HTTP server
when the user runs the service command.
A subcommand group for managing virtual machines. It is
used to create, start, stop, and interact with VMs that host
A subcommand group for managing Quadlet unit files. It is
used to install, list, print, and remove systemd unit files
A subcommand for generating shell completion scripts. It is
used to emit completion definitions for supported shells so
users can enable tab-completion for Podman commands.
Automated pipeline platform (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab
CI, …) that triggers container build, test, and deploy
